author: template-projects
name: Aspire starter add-on: Blazor front end
description: Adds a Blazor UI written once in a Razor Class Library and rendered by the hosts you ask for: a WebAssembly web host, a MAUI Blazor Hybrid mobile/desktop host, or both. Emits .scaffold/aspire-ui-blazor.wiring.md, which lists the solution and AppHost edits the scaffolding skill applies.

resource.description: The singular PascalCase name of the sample resource, e.g. Product. The scaffold's entity, controller, page and tests are named from it. The plural is this plus "s" - an irregular plural is a rename after scaffolding, not a second parameter. Pass the SAME value to every template in a scaffold, exactly like -n.

resourceLower.//: The lowercase form, for TypeScript identifiers, route paths and file names. A separate symbol because `replaces` is a literal substitution - unlike sourceName, it does not match case variants.

web.description: Include the Blazor WebAssembly host. This is the only client that genuinely needs CORS on the API.

maui.description: Include the MAUI Blazor Hybrid host for mobile and desktop. Requires the MAUI workload to build; the AppHost holds it back with WithExplicitStart so `aspire run` still works without it.

modifiers.//: CSS declares a grid property whose name contains this template's sourceName, so substitution would rewrite the property itself - the declaration then parses as unknown and the browser drops it, with no build error and nothing for bUnit to catch, because it does not evaluate CSS. The file needs no substitution of its own: its comments name neither a project nor the sample resource, and Assert-ResourceTokenSafe in stage.ps1 is what keeps it that way.
The WebAssembly host is the only deployable web front end here, so its Static Web App goes with it. The MAUI host provisions nothing - it is a client, not a workload.

modifiers.comment: The Pages RCL and its bUnit suite carry the whole UI; without a host to render them there is nothing to add.
